1.explanation: Both prism-sql.js and its minified counterpart define the SQL language’s comment and string patterns. The current comment pattern isn’t marked greedy (and/or is ordered after the string rule in a way that lets the escaped-quote string interferes with comment termination), so the “--” comment swallows the rest of the code block. Fixing the grammar in prism-sql.js (and then rebuilding or updating prism-sql.min.js) will correct SQL comment highlighting in this scenario.
1.bug_scenario: When you feed Prism a SQL snippet that contains a string with escaped single‐quotes (two single‐quotes to escape) and then immediately follow it with a “-- comment” line, Prism’s SQL grammar doesn’t close the comment at the end of that line. As a result, everything that follows (including the second INSERT) is highlighted as if it were part of the comment.

2.explanation: All of the SQL‐specific token definitions (for strings, comments, keywords, etc.) live in prism-sql.js. The regular expressions in that file determine how Prism recognizes and terminates single-quoted strings and line comments. Because the current comment regex doesn’t properly break out of a string literal after doubled quotes, the comment line isn’t matched correctly. The minified companion prism-sql.min.js also needs updating since it’s just a compressed copy of the same logic.
2.bug_scenario: When you feed Prism a SQL snippet that contains single‐quoted string literals with doubled quotes (e.g. ''hello world'') followed by a standalone line comment (-- this is a comment), Prism’s SQL grammar doesn’t correctly exit the string context before matching the comment. The result is that either the comment isn’t recognized properly or the string highlighting bleeds into it. In the screenshot you can see the value strings are closed in the code, but the next line’s “-- this is a comment” is not treated as a true comment (or is partially garbled) because the grammar is still stuck in string mode.
